quests.instruction: Two metro lines cross at one station. Which symbol best shows passengers changing from one line to the other?
quests.hint: Think of switching, not staying.
quests.explanation: An interchange lets passengers swap between lines, so they can reach more places without leaving the station. Big networks have many interchanges.
quests.funFact: Some interchange stations are so big that changing lines can mean a long walk.

quests.instruction: Which service skips small stations to reach big stations sooner?
quests.hint: It does not stop at every platform.
quests.explanation: An express service only stops at main stations, so it is faster. A local service stops at every station and serves smaller places.
quests.funFact: Express trains often use faster tracks so they can pass slower trains.

quests.instruction: What is the last stop at the end of a route called, where the vehicle finishes or turns around?
quests.hint: Think of a finishing line.
quests.explanation: The last stop is called the terminus, or end of the line. Passengers who stay on the vehicle must get off there.
quests.funFact: Some buses and trams turn around on a loop at the end of the line.

quests.instruction: Which time of day is called rush hour, when the most people travel to work and school?
quests.hint: People are heading out at the start of the day.
quests.explanation: Rush hour is when roads and public transport are busiest. Leaving a little earlier or later can mean a quieter journey.
quests.funFact: Many cities run extra buses and trains during rush hour.

quests.instruction: Which service is for people who travel when most other buses have stopped?
quests.hint: It runs after dark.
quests.explanation: Night services help people who work late or travel home after evening events when normal services have finished.
quests.funFact: Some big cities run night buses all night.

quests.instruction: Buses that come every ten minutes all day long are called what kind of service?
quests.hint: The buses repeat again and again.
quests.explanation: A frequent service means you do not need to check the timetable much, because another bus will be along soon. Planners use it on busy routes.
quests.funFact: Frequent services make it easier to change from one bus or train to another.

quests.instruction: Which airport screen shows the flights that are about to leave?
quests.hint: Look for the plane lifting off.
quests.explanation: Departure screens list flights with times and gate numbers. Arrival screens show planes that have landed.
quests.funFact: Airports update these screens as soon as a gate or time changes.

quests.instruction: Before boarding, bags go through a machine and officers check them. Which symbol could stand for this check?
quests.hint: Officers look closely inside.
quests.explanation: Security checks look for dangerous items so flights stay safe. Everyone, including crew, goes through them.
quests.funFact: Liquids over a certain size are not allowed in carry-on bags on many flights.

quests.instruction: Air traffic controllers watch the sky from a tall room above the airport. What is the tall building called?
quests.hint: It stands high so controllers can see all the runways.
quests.explanation: The control tower gives controllers a clear view of the runways and sky. They tell pilots when to take off, land, or wait.
quests.funFact: Controllers also use radar screens to see planes that are far away.

quests.instruction: At a port, which tall machine lifts big metal containers on and off ships?
quests.hint: It has a long arm and works right at the quayside.
quests.explanation: Port cranes can lift a loaded container in one go. Trucks and trains then carry it on.
quests.funFact: Some port cranes stand as tall as a 20-storey building.

quests.instruction: Where are many of the goods made that later travel by truck, train, and ship?
quests.hint: Machines make things here in large amounts.
quests.explanation: Goods start their journey at factories. Transport carries them to ports, warehouses, and shops.
quests.funFact: Factories are often near ports, rivers, or railways so goods can be moved easily.

quests.instruction: After a long journey from factory to port to warehouse, where do many goods end up so shoppers can buy them?
quests.hint: It is a place you visit to buy things.
quests.explanation: Shops are the last stop on the journey. A chain of ships, trains, and trucks brings goods there.
quests.funFact: A single product can pass through several countries before it reaches a shop.

quests.instruction: Some bridges and motorways charge a fee to help pay for building and looking after them. Which symbol could stand for this fee, called a toll?
quests.hint: Drivers pay it at a booth or with an electronic tag.
quests.explanation: A toll is money paid to use a particular road or bridge. It can help pay for repairs and new roads.
quests.funFact: Many toll roads now use electronic tags so cars do not have to stop.

quests.instruction: What do we call it when too many vehicles try to use a road at once and everything moves very slowly?
quests.hint: Think of a snail's speed.
quests.explanation: A traffic jam happens when there are more vehicles than the road can handle. Public transport, cycling, and walking can help reduce them.
quests.funFact: Traffic jams can build up even without an accident when many cars brake at once.

quests.instruction: A road has one lane painted for buses only. Which vehicle should use it?
quests.hint: It carries many passengers on a set route.
quests.explanation: Bus lanes let buses skip past traffic jams. This keeps public transport on time and attracts more riders.
quests.funFact: Some bus lanes can also be used by bicycles and taxis.

quests.instruction: Where railway tracks split and a train can be directed onto one path or the other, which symbol could show this?
quests.hint: Two arrows branch apart.
quests.explanation: Railway points are movable sections of track that guide trains onto different paths. Signals tell the driver which way the points are set.
quests.funFact: Points are moved by electric motors, and by hand in some places.

quests.instruction: Metro maps use different colours for each line. What helps passengers tell the lines apart?
quests.hint: Many bright shades are used.
quests.explanation: Colour-coding makes maps easy to read. You can follow your line's colour from start to finish.
quests.funFact: Many metro systems name their lines by colour, like the Red Line or Blue Line.

quests.instruction: The board says your train leaves from platform 3. Which number should you look for on the signs?
quests.hint: Match the number on the board to the number on the sign.
quests.explanation: Platform numbers show where each train stops. Check the screen again just before departure in case of a change.
quests.funFact: Platforms can change at short notice, so listen to announcements.

quests.instruction: Which lifts passengers between the platform and the street, helping people with wheelchairs and pushchairs?
quests.hint: It goes up and down inside a shaft.
quests.explanation: Station lifts help people who cannot use stairs, such as wheelchair users, people with heavy luggage, and families with prams.
quests.funFact: Station lifts have large buttons and sometimes beep to help everyone use them.

quests.instruction: Which sign-post style board guides people through a big station to platforms and exits?
quests.hint: It points the way.
quests.explanation: Clear signs let passengers find exits, platforms, and facilities quickly.
quests.funFact: Station signs use simple pictures so people who do not read the local language can follow them.

quests.instruction: Which symbol stands for signs and announcements in many languages?
quests.hint: It looks like a globe covered in lines.
quests.explanation: Airports and big stations welcome visitors from many countries. Signs in several languages help them find their way.
quests.funFact: Airports often use pictures and symbols that everyone can understand.

quests.instruction: A town closes its main street to cars so people can walk and shop safely. What does the street become?
quests.hint: People come here to buy things.
quests.explanation: Pedestrian streets are safe and pleasant for walking. Cars are kept out, although delivery vehicles may be allowed at set times.
quests.funFact: Many European towns have pedestrian-only centres.

quests.instruction: Which feature keeps cyclists separate from cars on a busy road?
quests.hint: It is a physical divider.
quests.explanation: A protected cycle lane has barriers or kerbs between bikes and cars. It helps more people feel safe cycling.
quests.funFact: Cities with protected cycle lanes often see more people riding bicycles.

quests.instruction: Many bus and train timetables change at weekends and on holidays. Which symbol shows which day a timetable is for?
quests.hint: It lists days and dates.
quests.explanation: Services often run less often at weekends and on holidays. Check the right day's timetable before you plan.
quests.funFact: Some timetables use different colours for weekday, Saturday, and Sunday services.

quests.instruction: A ferry leaves just after the train arrives, so passengers do not wait long. What have the planners created?
quests.hint: The services meet up neatly.
quests.explanation: A good connection lets passengers change from one service to the next without a long wait. It makes journeys easier.
quests.funFact: Some bus companies time departures to match train arrivals at busy stations.

quests.instruction: At a park-and-ride site, drivers leave their car and continue into the city by which vehicle?
quests.hint: It is a shared ride.
quests.explanation: Park-and-ride lets people drive part of the way and then use public transport. It reduces traffic and parking problems in busy centres.
quests.funFact: Park-and-ride sites are usually at the edge of a city, close to a main road.

quests.instruction: A village has few buses, so volunteers run a minibus to take older people to the doctor. Which vehicle is it?
quests.hint: It has seats for a small group.
quests.explanation: Community transport fills gaps where big services do not run. Volunteers and local groups often make it possible.
quests.funFact: Community minibuses often have ramps or lifts for wheelchairs.

quests.instruction: A city wants to carry more people along a busy road without adding more lanes. Which choice moves the most people in the same space?
quests.hint: One vehicle replaces many cars.
quests.explanation: A bus carries dozens of people in the space of two or three cars. Frequent buses can move far more people than cars on the same road.
quests.funFact: A single bus lane can carry many more people per hour than a lane of cars.

quests.instruction: Which technology helps a bus company show where each bus is on a live map?
quests.hint: Signals from space show where each bus is.
quests.explanation: Buses can carry a GPS device. Signals from satellites show the bus's position, which can be shared on an app.
quests.funFact: Live bus apps use GPS to tell you how many minutes until your bus arrives.

quests.instruction: Before planning a new bus route, planners need to know where which group of people live and want to go?
quests.hint: Think about who will ride.
quests.explanation: Transport exists to help people reach school, work, health care, and friends. Planners study where people live and need to go.
quests.funFact: Planners often count passengers and ask them about their needs to improve services.
